title: Catching up
goal: Catch up with a friend you haven't seen for a while: what you did at the weekend, what's new, "have you ever…?", and how long it's been since… or ago.
intro:
**بڑے عرصے بعد!** 'Long time no see!' — and then the questions start: **اور سناؤ**, **کوئی تازہ خبر؟**, **کہاں غائب تھے؟** Catching up is one of the most common conversations you will have, and it needs exactly the tenses you have been putting off.

This unit sorts out the three past forms you hear all the time — **گیا** 'went', **گیا ہے** 'has gone' and **گیا تھا** 'had gone / went (back then)' — together with the past continuous **کر رہا تھا** 'was doing', and how to say **for, since and ago** (**دو سال سے، دو سال پہلے، دو سال ہو گئے**). Watch for the big difference from English: 'I **have been** going to the gym for two months' is **present** in Urdu — **دو مہینے سے جم جا رہا ہوں**.

grammar.title: Did, has done, had done: گیا، گیا ہے، گیا تھا
grammar.body:
When you catch up you will use three past forms constantly:

**Simple past** — **گیا، کیا، دیکھا**: a finished event, often with a time word: کل میں نے فلم **دیکھی** 'I saw a film yesterday'.

**Present perfect** — past + **ہے / ہیں / ہوں / ہو**: something that has happened and matters now — news, results, experiences: میں نے نئی نوکری **شروع کی ہے** 'I've started a new job'; اس کی منگنی **ہو گئی ہے** 'she's got engaged'.

**Past perfect** — past + **تھا / تھی / تھے / تھیں**: 'had done', but Urdu also uses it for events further back that are over and done with — where English just says 'did': پچھلے سال ہم شمالی علاقوں میں **گئے تھے** 'we went up north last year'. It is also very common for something you did before the present conversation: میں نے فون **کیا تھا** 'I did call you'.

All three follow the rules of the simple past (unit 16): intransitive verbs agree with the subject; transitive verbs take **نے** and agree with the object: وہ آئی **ہے**، میں نے بریانی بنائی **ہے**، ہم نے دو فلمیں دیکھی **تھیں**.

**Ever / never:** **کبھی** + present perfect: کیا تم نے کبھی نہاری **کھائی ہے**؟ — **ہاں، کئی بار** / **نہیں، کبھی نہیں**. In the negative the ہے is usually dropped: میں کبھی وہاں نہیں **گیا**.

**The trap:** don't use the present perfect with a finished time such as کل or پچھلے ہفتے. 'I went yesterday' is **کل گیا** (or کل گیا تھا), never کل گیا ہے.

grammar.title: Was doing: the past continuous کر رہا تھا
grammar.body:
**Stem + رہا / رہی / رہے + تھا / تھی / تھے / تھیں** = 'was / were doing'. Like the present continuous, it agrees with the subject and **never takes نے**, even with transitive verbs: میں فلم دیکھ **رہا تھا** (not میں نے).

Use it for what was in progress at a moment, and as the **background** when something else happened in the simple past: میں سو **رہا تھا** جب تمہارا فون **آیا** 'I was asleep when you called'. Another very common way to link them is **کہ** 'when (suddenly)': میں دفتر جا رہا تھا **کہ** بارش شروع ہو گئی.

Asking what someone was up to: **کیا کر رہے تھے؟** — the past partner of **آج کل کیا کر رہے ہو؟** 'what are you up to these days?'.

Keep the three '-ing / habit' pasts apart:
**کرتا تھا** — used to do (habit, unit 26)
**کر رہا تھا** — was doing (in progress)
**کیا تھا** — had done / did (back then)

grammar.title: For, since, ago: سے، پہلے، and "it's been…"
grammar.body:
**سے** after a length of time or a starting point means **'for'** or **'since'**. If the thing is still going on, the verb is **present** — where English says 'have been':
میں دو سال **سے** یہاں رہ رہا **ہوں** 'I've been living here for two years'
وہ پچھلے مہینے **سے** جم جا رہی **ہے** 'she's been going to the gym since last month'
ہم بچپن **سے** دوست **ہیں** 'we've been friends since childhood'
Ask with **کب سے؟** 'since when / how long?'.

**پہلے** after a length of time = **'ago'**: دو سال **پہلے** 'two years ago', کچھ دن **پہلے** 'a few days ago'. (**… بعد** = '… later / after': بڑے عرصے **بعد**.)

**It's been…:** **ہو گئے / ہو گیا** — دو سال **ہو گئے** 'it's been two years'. To say since what, use the past form + **ہوئے**: ہمیں ملے **ہوئے** چھ مہینے ہو گئے 'it's been six months since we met'. Or just: **کتنا عرصہ ہو گیا!** 'it's been ages!'

**Ever since:** **جب سے** + present perfect: **جب سے** نوکری ملی ہے، بہت مصروف ہوں 'ever since I got the job I've been really busy'.

**The trap:** English 'have been … for' is **present** in Urdu. Saying رہ رہا **تھا** would mean you don't live there any more.

culture: Catching up in Pakistan starts with family, not with you: **گھر میں سب ٹھیک؟ امی ابو کیسے ہیں؟** comes before any news. **اور سناؤ** ('so, tell me') can be repeated several times in one conversation — it is a way of handing the other person the floor, not a real question, and **کچھ خاص نہیں** is a perfectly good answer. Friends who haven't been in touch get a playful telling-off — **کہاں غائب ہو؟ عید کا چاند ہو گئے ہو!** ('you've become the Eid moon', i.e. impossible to spot) — and the standard defence is **مصروفیت**. Expect questions English speakers might find personal: how much the new job pays, when you're getting married, why you've put on (or lost) weight. They are signs of interest, and you can deflect with a laugh: **بس، چل رہا ہے** 'oh, it's going'. Weddings, Eid and funerals are where most people actually catch up, and cricket is the universal safe topic — a Pakistan loss is always good for ten minutes. Among young people a lot of catching up happens over WhatsApp voice notes, ending with the promise everyone makes and nobody keeps: **رابطے میں رہنا!**

lessons.title: Long time no see!

tip.title: It's been ages: ہو گئے, پہلے
tip.body:
- 'It's been…' = **… ہو گئے / ہو گیا**: دو سال **ہو گئے**!
- Since what: **ملے ہوئے** دو سال ہو گئے 'two years since we met'.
- **پہلے** after a time = ago: دو سال **پہلے** · **بعد** = after: بڑے عرصے **بعد**.
- **سے** = for, since: مہینوں **سے** غائب ہو.
tip.pattern: time + پہلے (ago)  ·  time + سے (for)  ·  time + ہو گئے

tip.title: Did vs did (back then): گئے, گئے تھے
tip.body:
- A finished event: simple past — ویک اینڈ پر ہم سمندر پر **گئے**.
- Further back and over with, Urdu loves **past + تھا / تھی / تھے** where English just says 'did': دو سال پہلے ہم ٹرپ پر **گئے تھے**.
- Transitive verbs still take **نے**: ہم نے بہت مزے **کیے**.
tip.pattern: گئے (did)  ·  گئے تھے (did, back then / had done)

tip.title: News: ہو گئی ہے
tip.body:
- News that matters now uses the **present perfect**: past + **ہے / ہیں**: اس کی منگنی **ہو گئی ہے**!
- It agrees just like the simple past: بھائی کو ترقی **ملی** ہے (f.), داخلہ **مل گیا** ہے (m.).
- Not with a finished time like کل: کل منگنی **ہوئی** (not ہوئی ہے).

sentences.roman: us kī mangnī ho ga’ī hai!
sentences.en: She's got engaged!

lessons.title: Have you ever…?

tip.title: Have you ever…? کبھی … ہے؟
tip.body:
- 'Ever' = **کبھی** + present perfect: کیا تم نے کبھی بریانی **بنائی ہے**؟
- Answers: **ہاں، کئی بار** / **نہیں، کبھی نہیں**. In the negative ہے drops: میں کبھی نہیں **گیا**.
- **اب تک** 'so far': اب تک تین بار **گیا ہوں**.
tip.pattern: کیا + تم (نے) + کبھی + past + ہے / ہو؟

tip.title: Was doing: کر رہا تھا
tip.body:
- **Stem + رہا / رہی / رہے + تھا / تھی / تھے** = was / were doing.
- It agrees with the subject and **never takes نے**: میں فلم دیکھ **رہا تھا**.
- Background + event: میں سو **رہا تھا** جب تمہارا فون **آیا**.
tip.pattern: stem + رہا / رہی / رہے + تھا / تھی / تھے

lessons.title: How long have you been…?

tip.title: Have been … for: present + سے
tip.body:
- 'I **have been** doing it for / since…' is **present** in Urdu, with **سے**: دو مہینے **سے** جم جا رہا **ہوں**.
- Ask with **کب سے؟** 'since when?'
- **جب سے** = ever since: **جب سے** نوکری بدلی ہے…
- Trap: رہ رہا **تھا** would mean you don't any more.
